cases.title: Regional Fintech App Expansion into SEE Markets
cases.summary: Technical and operational readiness for launching a financial app in new SEE markets.
cases.problem: Expanding the app into new SEE markets meant meeting central bank and financial regulatory requirements in each jurisdiction, while steering committees, partner banks, legal teams and vendors all had to stay in sync.
cases.approach: Directed technical and operational readiness for the regional expansion and coordinated compliance requirements under central bank and financial regulatory frameworks. Ran regular alignment between steering committees, partner banking PMs and legal teams to keep milestones synchronized across jurisdictions, and coordinated external vendors, localized third-party integrations and security audit workflows.
my_role: Technical and operational readiness across target markets
Compliance coordination under central bank and financial regulation
Alignment of steering committees, partner banking PMs and legal teams
Vendor, third-party integration and security audit coordination
cases.outcome: By September 2026, testing was finished, the regulator had approved the project, and it was in final preparations for a phased production go-live.
context_points: Fintech app, regional rollout into SEE markets
Partner banks and regulators in several jurisdictions

cases.title: B2C Webshop for Slovenia
cases.summary: Preparing eKupi's expansion to other EU markets, starting with a new webshop for Slovenia.
cases.problem: eKupi planned to sell to consumers in other EU countries, starting with Slovenia, shipping from its warehouse in Croatia. That meant charging and reporting VAT under the EU One Stop Shop (OSS) scheme, with changes across the webshop, ERP, warehouse and reporting systems.
cases.approach:
Coordinated delivery of the localized webshop across business, legal, and technical workstreams. Translated requirements into stories, managed sprints, coordinated teams, and drove UAT and go-live readiness.

The planned scope covered a separate Slovenian webshop on the existing platform, with its own catalogue, promotions and content. In the ERP, it covered Slovenian VAT rates, separate invoices and quarterly OSS reporting. It also covered separating EU orders in the warehouse, shipping labels and tracking through the Slovenian post, and adding EU sales to BI reports.
my_role: Sprint planning, reporting, and scope control
cases.outcome: I coordinated the project through to its final phase and left the company before launch.
context_points: Workstreams: business, legal, technical
Sales model: consumers only, shipped from Croatia
VAT scheme: EU One Stop Shop (OSS)

cases.title: UNIQA Integration: Automated Warranty Policy Generation
cases.summary: Automation and workflow design connecting webshop and insurer systems.
cases.impact: Replaced a manual process with automatic insurance confirmations.
cases.problem: Warranty confirmations were created and sent by hand.
cases.approach: Designed the detailed logic, workflows, and data mapping for the integration between eKupi and UNIQA insurance systems. Aligned stakeholders and coordinated implementation, testing, deployment, and monitoring.
my_role: Logic, workflow and data mapping design
cases.outcome: Customers now receive their insurance confirmation by email automatically after purchase, replacing a process eKupi staff did by hand. Failed cases are visible to the team and can be retried.
context_points: Integration between the eKupi webshop and UNIQA insurance systems

cases.title: eKupi Dropshipment Model
cases.summary: Letting suppliers ship directly to customers while eKupi keeps control of the order.
cases.problem: eKupi wanted a scalable dropshipment model where products go straight from supplier to customer. eKupi had to keep control of orders, statuses and the customer experience, and the process had to stay separate from its own warehouse and logistics.
cases.approach:
Wrote the specification and coordinated development. It covered marking products for dropshipment through supplier imports, stock priority, a supplier portal with user roles for confirming availability and shipment, and new order statuses with retries and checks for the data exchange.

It also covered delivery pricing per supplier at checkout, payment rules, invoicing, returns and reporting. For partial deliveries, I set out the options with their trade-offs so the client could choose the right scope for the first version.
my_role: Options and trade-offs for client decisions
cases.outcome: I specified the model and coordinated development until I left the company. Dropshipment went live on the eKupi webshop after that.
context_points: Client: eKupi
Specified with a dedicated supplier portal

cases.title: Checkout A/B Testing
cases.summary: Giving the client's team a built-in way to test checkout changes.
cases.problem: The team needed a way to compare how customers respond to different delivery options at checkout, using real order data.
cases.approach:
Wrote the specification and coordinated development of A/B testing in the webshop's back office. Customers, both registered and guests, are automatically assigned to group A or B when they reach the delivery step of checkout.

The team can name a test, switch it on or off, choose the market and dates, and set the order of delivery options for each group. I also defined a report comparing the groups on orders, order value, delivery option selection and checkout completion.
cases.outcome: The A/B testing feature shipped, starting with the delivery step and designed to allow more scenarios later, such as payment methods.
context_points: Client: eKupi

cases.title: Supplier Price Protection
cases.summary: Stopping wrong supplier prices from reaching the webshop.
cases.problem: Suppliers update their own prices through file imports. A mistyped price could go straight through to the webshop, with a risk of selling products at the wrong price.
cases.approach:
Specified and coordinated price limits that can be set separately for each supplier, covering price increases and decreases on purchase and recommended prices. An import that goes over a limit is blocked and the product is taken off sale until someone checks it.

Named contacts receive a regular email report of blocked prices. Correcting a price is a deliberate step, followed by manual re-approval of the product.
my_role: User guide for the client's team
cases.outcome: Suspicious supplier prices are stopped before customers can buy at them, and the team gets a clear list to review. The client was pleased with the result.
context_points: Client: eKupi
Limits adjustable per supplier

cases.title: Delivery Zone Rules
cases.summary: Controlling delivery prices and availability by postal code and product type.
cases.problem: Carriers' delivery prices kept changing, and some areas, such as remote islands, had no carrier for large goods. The webshop needed a way to reflect this at checkout without blocking customers from everything else.
cases.approach:
Specified and coordinated postal-code zones that the client's team can manage themselves. A zone can carry a higher delivery price for certain categories or exclude a delivery method for certain categories and products.

I also defined what happens when rules conflict: an exclusion always wins, including over forced delivery settings and promotions.
my_role: Requirements and business rules, including rule priorities
User guide for the client's team
cases.outcome: Customers in restricted zones can still order lighter products or use a pick-up point, and delivery options at checkout match what carriers can do.
context_points: Client: eKupi
Rules also apply in the one-page checkout

cases.title: Anchor Price Compliance
cases.summary: Showing the legally required anchor price across the webshop.
cases.problem: A legal requirement in force from 15 May 2025 meant webshops had to show an anchor price for certain FMCG products, wherever a customer could add the product to the cart.
cases.approach:
Specified and coordinated how the anchor price and its date move from the pricing system to the webshop and appear on product, category and search pages. The price shows only when both values exist, and the client's team can switch it on by category, with subcategories following.

I tested the behaviour against documented scenarios, such as new products and later price changes.
my_role: Requirements based on the legal obligation
Coordination across pricing and webshop teams
cases.outcome: Anchor prices went live by the legal deadline of 15 May 2025 on the required pages for the selected categories.
context_points: Client: eKupi
Legal requirement in force from 15 May 2025

cases.title: Returns Chatbot
cases.summary: Letting eKupi customers start a return through a chatbot.
cases.problem: eKupi wanted customers to be able to start a return through a chatbot, connected securely to the webshop's existing returns process.
cases.approach:
Worked as the business analyst: gathered user requirements, opened tickets, communicated with developers and vendors, and tested on the test environment and in production.

The proposed solution reused the existing returns process, added a check that an order belongs to the customer, and let customers approve or reject a chatbot-created request through a link sent by email.
my_role: Tickets and communication with developers and vendors
Testing on the test environment and in production
context_points: Client: eKupi

cases.title: Abrakadabra Mobile App Delivery
cases.summary: Delivering a mobile app connected to the Abrakadabra webshop, built with an external vendor.
cases.problem: Abrakadabra wanted a mobile app that worked from the same products, prices, customer accounts and orders as its webshop. An external vendor would build it, so requirements, data and priorities had to stay clear across both teams while stakeholders' needs changed.
cases.approach:
Organized Agile ceremonies and drove requirements gathering together with stakeholders. Prioritized the backlog, clarified requirements quickly, and handled change requests promptly to avoid delays while meeting core business requirements.

Wrote the REST API specification for what the app needed, from registered and guest customers to categories, products and customer orders. Gave the vendor's team guidance on webshop content and coupons. Contacted the payment gateway vendor for the materials needed for the integration, then tested payments, promotions and the other activities needed for go-live.
my_role: REST API specification and vendor coordination
cases.outcome: The app was delivered within scope and went live for a closed user group.
context_points: Alongside the app, owned the department's technology strategy and budget for B2C e-commerce, reporting metrics and risks to senior leadership
Mentored engineers through training workshops and best-practice documentation

cases.title: Euro Changeover for the Abrakadabra Webshop
cases.summary: Taking the webshop and business systems from kuna to euro on a fixed national deadline.
cases.problem: Croatia adopted the euro on 1 January 2023, and the date could not move. Regulation also required prices in both currencies from 5 September 2022, with the fixed exchange rate, and the rules changed in stages. Orders, stock and deliveries had to keep running throughout.
cases.approach:
Coordinated A007's part of the Fortenova Group changeover, working to a group-wide transition plan with regular readiness reporting.

Specified the dual price display: three phases, and how prices should appear at each customer touchpoint, from product carousels and product pages to the cart, checkout, order history and order confirmation emails. This included the rounding rules and labels the team could edit in the back office.

The ERP ran in parallel in kuna and euro ahead of the changeover, with products, prices, stock and open orders migrated at the end of December.
my_role: Coordinating A007's part of the group changeover
Translating the regulation into requirements and display rules
Coordination across webshop, ERP and operations
cases.outcome: The dual price display went live on 5 September 2022, and the business moved to the euro as its official currency on 1 January 2023.
context_points: Phase 1, from 5 Sep 2022: kuna as main currency, euro secondary
Phase 2, from 1 Jan 2023: euro as main currency, kuna secondary
Phase 3, after 31 Dec 2023: euro only
Fixed conversion rate: 1 EUR = 7.53450 HRK
Systems: SAP Commerce (Hybris), SAP Business One

cases.title: Loyalty Partner Integrations
cases.summary: Connecting the Abrakadabra webshop to the Tokić and MultiPlus loyalty programmes.
cases.problem: Tokić's loyalty club customers (Tklub and Bklub) were to redeem their points for Abrakadabra products, which required reliable product, price and stock data and clear visibility of the resulting orders. Separately, joining the MultiPlus programme meant connecting the webshop to its systems so that online purchases could count for members.
cases.approach:
Led the Tokić project and proposed the solution: an XML product feed covering product names, descriptions, images, categories, prices and stock, a category structure and product list aligned with the partner, checkout logic for redeeming points, and order reporting with order and delivery status and tracking IDs. Coordinated two development teams, worked with Tokić's IT vendor during implementation and tested the result.

For MultiPlus, upgraded the system so customers could collect loyalty points and use them on the webshop, working from the partner's interface specification.
my_role: Led the Tokić project and proposed the solution
Contact with Tokić's IT vendor during implementation
MultiPlus system upgrade for collecting and using points
cases.outcome: The Tokić integration went live, with a shared product feed and order report giving both sides the same view of products and orders. The MultiPlus upgrade also went live, so customers could collect and use loyalty points on the webshop.
context_points: Partners: Tokić, MultiPlus
Tokić project: Apr 2023 to Jun 2023

cases.title: Dropshipping + Logistics Integrations
cases.summary: Selling a partner's products through the Abrakadabra webshop with dropshipping, alongside several logistics partners.
cases.problem: Abrakadabra wanted to sell TISAK's products on its webshop through dropshipping, so product data, stock and order status had to stay in sync between two companies' systems. It also needed several logistics partners working within the same delivery process.
cases.approach:
Integrated dropshipping with TISAK: wrote the XML feed specification for products, stock and prices, and the order process between the two companies, with scenarios for full availability, changed quantities and cancelled orders, including who gets notified. Prepared test scenarios and coordinated testing.

Coordinated the logistics partners GLS, Milšped, Labaš and CRO Express, managing timelines and partner communication.
my_role: XML feed and order process specification
cases.outcome: Dropshipping with TISAK went live on the webshop, and the logistics partners were integrated into its delivery flow.
context_points: TISAK: Sep 2022 to Feb 2023
GLS, Milšped and Labaš live in 2023; CRO Express live in 2024
Data exchange: XML feed

cases.title: Outdoor Parcel Lockers
cases.summary: Bringing 24/7 outdoor pick-up points to eKupi customers.
cases.problem: With online purchasing growing, eKupi introduced outdoor parcel lockers offering pick-up locations available around the clock, which required coordinating several stakeholders.
cases.approach:
Tested hardware and software at certain phases and configured new lockers' software. Wrote instructions for the couriers delivering to the lockers, documented the functionality and transferred the knowledge to colleagues.

Supported the lockers through troubleshooting, adjusting functionality and monitoring.
cases.outcome: The outdoor parcel lockers went live.
context_points: Pick-up available 24/7

cases.title: Web Kredit on eKupi.rs
cases.summary: Letting customers in Serbia pay in instalments through a web loan with Raiffeisen bank.
cases.problem: eKupi.rs wanted to offer payment in instalments through a web loan, which meant the webshop and the bank's systems had to work together reliably at checkout.
cases.approach: Tested the delivered functionality and gave developers the feedback they needed, working with colleagues at eKupi Serbia. Communicated with Raiffeisen's IT department, and documented the guide the development team could use for later back-end changes.
my_role: Contact with the bank's IT department
cases.outcome: Web Kredit went live on eKupi.rs.
context_points: Partner: Raiffeisen bank
Market: Serbia

cases.title: Platform Training and Documentation
cases.summary: Helping teams work confidently in the eCommerce platform through guides and role-based workshops.
cases.problem: Category managers, business analysts, marketing, customer support and procurement all had to work in several connected systems. When M SAN's B2B team needed the same skills, much of what eKupi's B2C teams used carried over.
cases.approach:
Wrote and maintained dozens of user guides, published on the internal portal, covering products, pricing, promotions, web content, orders, returns and customer support tools.

Designed and ran role-based workshops for the eKupi team in 2019 and for M SAN's B2B team in 2020, planned by department and system, with hands-on exercises and a practical knowledge check. Trained close to 200 colleagues across five countries: Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro and North Macedonia.
cases.outcome: Teams could work more independently in the systems, with fewer support questions.
context_points: Audience: category managers, business analysts, marketing, customer support, procurement
Workshops for the eKupi and M SAN B2B teams

cases.title: eKupi Migration to SAP eCommerce Platform
cases.summary: Multi-market migration with data integrity, configuration, and enablement.
cases.impact: Webshops in 5 markets migrated to SAP eCommerce without data loss.
cases.problem: Several regional webshops needed platform migration while protecting data integrity and minimizing disruption.
cases.approach: Was a member of the team that migrated eKupi's webshops to the SAP eCommerce platform across five markets. Migrated and validated product and content data, configured payment methods, delivery options and product displays, tested order processes, and supported teams with documentation.
my_role: Coordination with colleagues across the regional teams
Migration validation and content integrity checks
Site configuration: payments, delivery options, product displays
Training and documentation through internal portal
cases.outcome: All five webshops moved to one platform.
context_points: Markets: Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia
Platform: SAP eCommerce
results: Products and content moved without data loss, including images, descriptions and pricing

cases.title: Multi-Brand Webshop: Specification, Vendor Selection and Cost Model
cases.summary: Specification, vendor selection and cost modelling for a multi-brand webshop in CEE/SEE markets.
cases.problem: These consumer brands were sold only in physical stores or by phone. The company wanted one multilingual online store, built for mobile first, that could serve several countries with different legal, payment and delivery requirements.
cases.approach:
When the company considered moving from a vendor build to in-house Shopify, I prepared a CAPEX and OPEX cost model comparing both options and presented the results to decision-makers. The model showed Shopify would cost more than the vendor's custom solution.

Before that, I wrote the functional specification and broke the project down into epics, from design and checkout to payments and SEO. I also reviewed legal requirements across six countries, shortlisted payment providers and evaluated nine agencies.
my_role: Legal and payment requirements across markets
cases.outcome: I left about a month into the in-house Shopify phase. The team continued for almost six months and reached a test environment, and the company was then shut down before production launch.
context_points: Company: Home of Brands, created by Kenty Adria
Brands: Delimano, Rovus, Wellneo, Schmidler, Walkmaxx
Planned first markets: Croatia, Slovenia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina

cases.title: Personal Portfolio Website
cases.summary: A portfolio site built with Claude Code that I can update myself, with project claims reviewed against my own documents.
cases.problem: My work was spread across a CV, LinkedIn and years of project documents. I wanted one place where visitors could quickly find relevant projects, and I wanted to edit it without touching code.
cases.approach:
Set the direction and made the decisions on content and structure, with Claude Code writing the code. Reviewed changes before publishing.

Used Claude to go through my source documents, compare the projects with my CV and LinkedIn, and rewrite them, then reviewed the claims and removed what couldn't be verified. Kept client documents' details out of the public pages.
cases.outcome: A live static site with filters by area, light and dark themes and a phone layout. Content can be edited through a CMS without code.
context_points: First version Dec 2025; rebuilt Oct to Nov 2026
Built with: Claude Code, HTML, CSS, JavaScript
Hosting and editing: GitHub Pages, Pages CMS
Claude wrote the code; decisions, facts and final review were mine
